items.title: Treasuries Now Offer 2.66% Above Inflation. Are Dividend Stocks in Trouble?
items.summary: Real yields hit a level that crushed income stocks once before, and one dividend name is already repeating the old script. Which holdings sat out the damage this time, and what single number could turn the tide again?

items.title: Why Is WPP (LSE:WPP) Challenging Agency Pitch Rules In Public?
items.summary: WPP (LSE:WPP) and rival Publicis have entered a rare public dispute over how major advertising accounts are awarded. The clash focuses on so called pitchless wins for global clients such as Coca Cola and PepsiCo and the fairness of such processes. Both groups are using the row to question each other's approach to client acquisition, technology use and internal operating models. items.title: I Bonds Pay 5.51%. Why Retirees Might Still Prefer Dividend Stocks
items.summary: A Treasury-backed bond out-yields Coca-Cola and Qualcomm by a wide margin, yet retirees keep buying dividend stocks. Between lockups, state taxes, and a missing paycheck, the real math may surprise you.

items.title: Meet Wall Street’s Safest Dividend Stocks: 3 Companies That Have Paid Through Recessions, Wars and Market Crashes
items.summary: One of these three dividend payers started out selling candles and soap, another grew out of Rockefeller's Standard Oil. Each carries a hidden risk, and one stock looks pricey enough to challenge its own safe reputation.
